report: The brain tissue section shows various cells with round to oval nuclei, suggestive of neurons and glial cells, and areas of dense and sparse cellularity, likely representing neuropil. Pink-staining structures hint at possible amyloid plaques, characteristic of Alzheimer's disease. Clear spaces suggest vasculature or preparation artifacts. No inflammation or necrosis is evident. Further staining is needed for definitive diagnosis.

evidence.title: Various antibody clones of Napsin A, TTF-1, and p40 in non-small cell lung carcinoma
evidence.text: This tissue-microarray study evaluated CK5, p63, and p40 as squamous markers and Napsin A and TTF-1 as lung adenocarcinoma markers. Reported performance varied by marker and antibody clone, and combining Napsin A with TTF-1 improved sensitivity.

evidence.title: Educational case: basal cell carcinoma and its histologic differential
evidence.text: Basal cell carcinoma shows dermal islands of basophilic tumor cells with peripheral nuclear palisading, stromal retraction, and loose mucinous stroma. Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma shows invasive islands of pleomorphic keratinocytes arising from the epidermis with prominent nucleoli and increased mitoses. Melanoma can show irregular nests and single pleomorphic pigmented melanocytes within the epidermis and dermis.

evidence.title: Immunostaining for TTF-1, Napsin A, p40, and cytokeratin 5 aids differential diagnosis of NSCLC
evidence.text: The study compared marker combinations for separating lung adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma. TTF-1 and Napsin A supported adenocarcinoma, while p40 and CK5 supported squamous differentiation; the combined panel was more informative than a single stain.

evidence.title: Histologic features of cytomegalovirus esophagitis
evidence.text: CMV cytopathic effect is typically found in endothelial and stromal cells at the ulcer base. Histology may show cytomegaly, eccentrically positioned basophilic intranuclear inclusions surrounded by a clear halo, pale perinuclear regions, and an owl-eye appearance; CMV immunohistochemistry can confirm infected cells.

evidence.title: Colorectal carcinoma: pathologic aspects
evidence.text: Colorectal adenocarcinoma commonly forms malignant glands. Invasion can be accompanied by desmoplastic stroma, and glandular lumina frequently contain characteristic dirty necrosis. Benign colonic mucosa retains orderly crypt architecture and mature goblet cells without dysplasia.

review.assessment: The vision models consistently predict 'lower-grade glioma', which aligns with the report's description of brain tissue and lack of necrosis, though the report suggests a non-neoplastic neurodegenerative process (Alzheimer's).
rationale: The de-identified report describes brain tissue with round to oval nuclei and neuropil, which matches the case-specific prompt for lower-grade glioma.
The report explicitly states 'no inflammation or necrosis is evident', a key feature of lower-grade gliomas compared to higher-grade malignancies.
All four vision models (CONCH, MUSK, PLIP, QUILTNET) reached a consensus on lower-grade glioma across both baseline and prompted outputs.
discrepancies: The pathology report suggests the presence of amyloid plaques characteristic of Alzheimer's disease, which is a neurodegenerative condition rather than a glioma.
recommended_review: Human neuropathologist review to differentiate between a low-grade glial neoplasm and Alzheimer's disease pathology.
Amyloid-beta and tau protein immunohistochemical staining.
limitations: Retrieved literature provided no relevant evidence for brain pathology or gliomas, focusing instead on lung, skin, and colorectal cancers.
Model confidence scores are numerically low (0.12-0.17), indicating high uncertainty despite the consensus.
